items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β},
  t.card < s.card → ∀ {f : α → β}, Set.MapsTo f ↑s ↑t → ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ s, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y
items.informal_description: If the cardinality of a finite set $ t $ is strictly less than that of another finite set $ s $, and if a function $ f $ maps $ s $ to $ t $, then there exist distinct elements $ x $ and $ y $ in $ s $ such that $ f(x) = f(y) $. This is a direct application of the pigeonhole principle to finite sets.

items.informal_name: Existence of a Small Fiber Given $|s| < |t| \cdot n$
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [inst : DecidableEq β] {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β} {f : α → β} {n : ℕ},
  s.card < t.card * n → ∃ y ∈ t, {x ∈ s | f x = y}.card < n
items.informal_description: For finite sets $s$ and $t$, if the cardinality of $s$ is strictly less than $n$ times the cardinality of $t$, then there exists an element $y \in t$ such that the number of elements $x \in s$ satisfying $f(x) = y$ is strictly less than $n$.
